they seize one prisoner of war and one woman of the land
(The king) takes the festive garments off his body
they clothe the man in them
the woman they clothe in the festive garments of a woman
I have given him an adorned man as his substitute
But to the woman he speaks (the words) about a female deity
they drive up one bull and one [ewe] of the enemy land itself
fitted with ašuša-(rings?) at his ears
Red wool, green wool, black wool (and) [white wool] he draws out of the king's mouth
I have given you an [adorned], ašuša-(ringed), approved(?) [bull]
Afterwards (they bring) the adorned ewe, and he speaks (the words) about a female deity
they drive the ašuša-(ringed) bull [and the ewe] ahead of [the prisoner] and the woman
